answer: The gale report exposes the merge explicitly at each wander. Because of that, an attacker who spins up 299 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 175 times the capital for one share. The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. The fee repeats 19 times over. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
